resources.string: Either the off switch is on or the fix hasn\'t started yet. The correction log shows which.
Fix is ON (root mode, not installed)
The installer only works on the Sonim XP3800 with Android 8.1.\n\nThis phone: Android %1$s, XP3800 keypad %2$s.

Installing needs root, but only for the install. The fix runs without root afterwards.\n\nGet root first (for example with Root Manager), then come back. Or install from a computer: see the README on GitHub.
Undo needs root. Without root you can still turn the fix off (Turn off / on), or flash your system backup over EDL.
The fix is already installed. To reinstall, use Undo, restart the phone, then install again.

Before you start, have a backup of the system partition and an EDL flashing setup, in case the phone won't boot.

The app will:
• Back up the stock policy to /data/local/tmp/kd_dry/stock and /sdcard/keydebounce-backup. Copy it to your computer: Undo needs it.
• Compile the new policy the way the phone does at boot, and stop without changing anything if that fails.
• Install the daemon and the policy.

Afterwards, before you restart: remove root, or disable apps that ask for root at startup (such as Lucky Patcher). With the fix installed, getting root crashed the phone on almost every attempt.
The fix isn\'t installed, so there\'s nothing to undo.

This restores the stock policy from the backup made when the fix was installed (or from policy-backup/ copied to /data/local/tmp/kd_dry/stock), removes the daemon, and then asks you to restart.\n\nWarning: with the fix installed, getting root crashed the phone on almost every attempt during testing. If the phone restarts, try again. If it keeps failing, flash your system backup over EDL.
Turn the fix off or on

From a computer (no root needed):

Off:
adb shell touch /data/local/tmp/keydebounce.off
adb reboot

On:
adb shell rm /data/local/tmp/keydebounce.off
adb reboot

When the fix is off, the keypad works as it did before.
The fix isn\'t installed. If you run it in root mode, use Run with root (no install) → Stop, and turn off Start at boot.
With root, the app can do this now, without a restart. With the fix installed, getting root crashed the phone on almost every attempt during testing.

Starts the filter through root, the way Shizuku starts its server. Nothing in /system or the SELinux policy changes, and it stops when the phone restarts.

Start at boot is %1$s. When it's on, the app asks for root after each restart to start the filter again.

The root has to allow access to the keypad and /dev/uinput (Magisk does). If it doesn't, the output shows why.
The fix is installed, so it already starts at boot. Root mode is for phones without the install.
Root mode needs root. Without root, the only option is the permanent install from a computer (see the README on GitHub).
Start at boot is on. After a restart the app asks for root and starts the filter.
No result: root wasn\'t available, was refused, or stopped partway. If there\'s no output above, nothing was changed; otherwise the output shows how far it got.
It stopped at the step shown above. Everything before that step is listed in the output.
This screen was restarted, so the command wasn\'t run again. Check the status on the main screen.
Dry run passed. Nothing on the phone was changed.

Installed.

Before you restart: remove root, or disable apps that ask for root at startup (such as Lucky Patcher).

Copy /sdcard/keydebounce-backup to your computer. Undo needs it.

Then restart the phone to turn the fix on.
Removed. Restart the phone to finish.
Off. The keypad works unfiltered now, and the fix stays off after restarts until you turn it back on.
Running. It stops when the phone restarts, unless Start at boot is on.

Before restarting, remove root or disable apps that ask for root at startup (such as Lucky Patcher). With the fix installed, an app that asks for root at startup can cause a reboot loop.\n\nIf you\'re removing root first, restart with the power key afterwards.
Restart to finish removing the fix.
Type in the box. Every press is listed below, newest first. The extra digit comes from overlaps (a key pressed while another is held); with the fix on there should be none. Press Back to exit.

The app needs a one-time permission to read the log. From a computer:

adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.READ_LOGS
adb shell am force-stop %1$s

Then open the app again.
Counts cover what\'s still in the phone\'s log, usually since the last restart.
At its last start the off switch was on, so it exited.
No keydebounce lines in the log yet. Startup messages can get pushed out of the log during boot.
